lines: Jordan Rivera
+1 (555) 010-2287 | jordan.rivera@example.com | example.com/in/jrivera
Date of birth: 22 May 1997 | Nationality: Chilean
EDUCATION
Northgate University | M.P.H. in Biostatistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Meridian Heart Institute | Clinical Research Coordinator | Metro City, USA | Sep 2022 - Jul 2025
- Coordinated a 3-site randomized trial of a nurse-led discharge program for 640 heart-failure patients, finishing enrollment 4 months early with 94% of follow-up visits completed.
- Cut data-entry errors in the trial database from 6.1% to 1.8% of fields by adding range checks and double entry for the primary outcome.
- Estimated median survival in each arm by averaging the follow-up time of patients who died, excluding censored patients.
- Reconciling adverse-event reports across three sites, coding them to MedDRA terms and cross-checking them against pharmacy records each week, cut unresolved safety queries from 45 to 6.
- Presented monthly safety reports to the data monitoring committee, and all 4 reviews passed without a protocol change.
- Trained 9 site nurses on the consent process and outcome forms, and no consent deviations were found at the final audit.
Northgate University Hospital | Research Assistant | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Aug 2022
- Randomized patients by assigning those admitted on odd-numbered days to the program and even-numbered days to usual care.
- Interviewed 25 patients about missed clinic visits; the findings added text reminders that cut no-shows from 18% to 11%.
- Wrote the study's data dictionary for 180 variables, which the next two cohort studies reused.

- Cleaned and merged lab data from two hospital systems while also scheduling participant visits, ordering study supplies, taking minutes at lab meetings and covering the front desk, which resolved 1,200 mismatched patient identifiers.
PROJECTS
Asthma Readmission Analysis | Independent Project | R | Jan 2025 - Present
- Harnessed cutting-edge analytics to deliver transformative, patient-centered insights into respiratory health outcomes.
- Found that 7-day follow-up cut readmission from 12% to 8%, a 50% reduction, after adjusting for age and insurance.
- Raised the survey response rate by 20% with SMS reminders, from 35% to 55% of invited residents.
Community Health Survey | Volunteer, Team of 5 | REDCap | Mar 2020 - Aug 2020
- Designed a 30-question community health survey and collected 1,100 responses, giving the clinic its first estimate of uninsured residents by neighborhood.
- The survey was translated into Spanish and piloted with 20 residents before launch.
- Wrote the survey's data codebook, which the clinic used for its follow-up survey the next year.
SKILLS
Tools: R, REDCap
Methods: randomized trials, regression, mixed-effects models, survey design

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is generally unnecessary on a US resume and can invite age bias.

items.says: Remove nationality unless it is relevant or needed to clarify work authorization.
items.because: Work authorization should be stated directly rather than inferred from nationality.

items.says: Use the degree’s official name if “M.P.H. in Biostatistics” is not how the university confers it.
Consider adding relevant coursework, a thesis, or an academic distinction.
items.because: It should strengthen your fit and be substantiated.

items.says: Clarify your personal responsibilities in the three-site trial.
Specify what “4 months early” is measured against.
items.because: The enrollment timeline should be documentable.

items.says: Give the denominator and time point for the 94% visit-completion figure.
items.because: Completed follow-up visits are different from participants retained.

items.says: Define how data-entry errors were measured, including the sample or audit period.
items.because: The field-level percentages lack context needed to assess them.

items.says: Distinguish the impact of range checks from that of double entry.
items.because: The current wording does not separate their effects.

items.says: Averaging follow-up times only among patients who died is not a valid median-survival estimate.
items.because: Excluding censored patients can produce a biased and misleading result.

items.says: Fix the opening participle’s tense.
items.because: The surrounding entries describe completed work.

items.says: Define what unresolved safety queries counts and over what period.
Make the reconciliation work and its result easier to distinguish.
items.because: The current sentence makes them hard to separate.

items.says: Explain what “all 4 reviews passed” means.
items.because: It is vague and may overstate what committee review means.

items.says: Do not treat the absence of a protocol change as proof of success.
items.because: It does not establish that the reports or trial were successful.

items.says: State your contribution to the safety reports clearly.
Clarify whether you trained all nine nurses yourself or contributed to their training.
Specify the audit scope behind “no consent deviations.”
Avoid implying that training alone caused the absence of consent deviations.
items.because: The connection needs to be demonstrated.

items.says: Do not describe odd/even admission-day assignment as randomization.
items.because: Admission day is predictable and may be associated with patient or staffing differences.

items.says: Accurately characterize the assignment design and disclose its limitation.
items.because: The groups should not be treated as randomized in a later analysis.

items.says: Explain how the 25 interviewees were selected.
Specify when the no-show rates were measured and whether the decrease followed the reminders.
Do not claim the interviews and reminders caused the reduction without supporting study design.
items.because: The current wording suggests a causal connection.

items.says: Clarify whether you defined, documented, or maintained the variables.
items.because: That would show the scale and your contribution.

items.says: Verify the claim that two later studies reused the data dictionary.
Separate the analytical work from the unrelated administrative duties.
items.because: The combined sentence makes the data-cleaning result easy to miss.

items.says: Explain what the 1,200 mismatched identifiers were and how matches were resolved or verified.
items.because: Identifier reconciliation does not necessarily mean resolving 1,200 distinct patient records.

items.says: Remove the generic promotional bullet.
items.because: It says nothing about the analysis, methods, data, or your contribution.

items.says: Correct the claimed 50% reduction.
items.because: A decrease from 12% to 8% is 4 percentage points or 33.3% relative.

items.says: Do not imply that follow-up caused the lower readmission rate without supporting evidence.
items.because: Adjustment for age and insurance alone does not establish causation.

items.says: Include the sample size, data source, outcome definition, model or method, and available uncertainty estimates.
items.because: They provide context for assessing the result.

items.says: Clarify what “7-day follow-up” means.
Correct “20%” to a 20-percentage-point increase.
items.because: Moving from 35% to 55% is not a 20% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify the number invited, time period, and definition of a response.
Say whether there was a comparison group.
Do not imply SMS caused the increase without a supporting design.
Clarify that the asthma project was independent rather than Meridian work, if accurate.
items.because: Its dates overlap with the Meridian role.

items.says: Be prepared to explain the asthma project’s data source, analysis, and individual contribution.
Clarify whether the 1,100 responses were complete.
Explain how residents were recruited and which neighborhoods or population they represent.
items.because: Representativeness depends on the sampling and response process.

items.says: State what you personally did in the translation and pilot, if responsible.
Do not imply the 20-person pilot validated the survey.
items.because: It may help identify issues, but does not alone establish validation.

items.says: Clarify your role in creating the codebook and how its reuse was confirmed.
Distinguish reuse with changes from unchanged adoption, if applicable.
Show specific R and REDCap capabilities you can demonstrate.
items.because: The resume does not show what you can do in either tool.

items.says: Connect regression and mixed-effects models to real work or projects.
items.because: The experience bullets do not demonstrate them clearly.

items.says: Ensure the listed methods reflect your actual training and experience.
items.because: The survival-analysis bullet raises questions about that fit.
